question: A regular hexagon is inscribed in a circle of radius \(10\) inches. Its area is:
solution:
Join the circle's center to all six vertices. These segments divide the regular hexagon into six triangles with equal central angles, each measuring \(360^\circ/6=60^\circ\). Each triangle has two radii of length \(10\), so it is an isosceles triangle with a \(60^\circ\) vertex angle and therefore is equilateral.

An altitude of one such triangle bisects its base into lengths \(5\) and \(5\). By the Pythagorean theorem, its positive altitude \(h\) is
\[
h=\sqrt{10^2-5^2}=\sqrt{75}=5\sqrt3.
\]
The six triangles cover the hexagon without overlapping interiors. Its area is therefore
\[
6\left(\frac12\cdot10\cdot5\sqrt3\right)
=150\sqrt3
\]
square inches, choice A.
